d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 4. The Temperate Region
d.notions: Deciduous forest, coniferous forest, Mediterranean vegetation, temperate grassland, brown forest soil, podzol, chernozem.
d.focus: Characteristics of the soils and vegetation of the temperate region.
d.competence: Learners are able to recognise pine and eucalyptus trees planted in Cameroon as temperate trees, and explain why temperate grasslands feed the world.
objectives: Describe the vegetation of the three types of temperate region.
Explain how temperate plants are adapted to their climate.
recall: The temperate region lies between 30° and 60° north and south of the Equator.
It has four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
Its three types of climate are oceanic, Mediterranean and continental.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: the colour of European forests in autumn.
situation: On a trip to Europe, Samuel sees a forest in November. All the trees have yellow and red leaves, and many leaves are falling to the ground. In January, the trees are completely bare.
In Garoua, many trees also lose their leaves, but in the dry season, not because of cold. Samuel wonders why European trees lose their leaves in winter.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Samuel does not understand why European trees lose their leaves in winter.
When do the trees of Garoua lose their leaves?
The trees of Garoua lose their leaves in the dry season.
What can Samuel do to find the answer?
He can ask his geography teacher, read his textbook, or compare the climates of Garoua and Europe.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to know the forests, grasslands and soils of the temperate region.

qa.q: In Western Europe, trees like the oak and the beech lose their leaves in autumn. Why?
qa.a: In winter, it is cold and the ground may freeze, so trees cannot get water. They lose their leaves to save water. They are deciduous trees.

qa.q: Further north, trees like the pine and the spruce keep their needle-shaped leaves in winter. How do their leaves help them?
qa.a: Their thin, waxy needles lose little water, and their cone shape lets the snow slide off. They are coniferous trees.

qa.q: The olive tree of the Mediterranean has small, thick, waxy leaves. How does this help it in the hot, dry summer?
qa.a: Small, thick, waxy leaves lose very little water. Mediterranean plants also have long roots and thick bark, like the cork oak.

qa.q: In the Prairies and the Steppes, there are almost no trees, only short grass. Why?
qa.a: The rainfall is low and the winters are very cold, so trees cannot grow well. Only short grass grows.

sum.title: I. Vegetation
sum.intro: The vegetation of the temperate region has the following types:
items: A. Deciduous Forest
In the oceanic climate, trees such as the oak, the beech and the ash lose their leaves in autumn to survive the winter.
B. Coniferous Forest
In the colder parts, trees such as the pine and the spruce keep their needle-shaped leaves all year and have cones.
C. Mediterranean Vegetation
Olive trees, cork oaks and bushes (maquis) have small, waxy leaves, long roots and thick bark to resist summer drought.
D. Temperate Grasslands
In the continental interiors, short grasses grow with few trees: the Prairies, the Steppes, the Pampas and the Veld.

qa.q: Every autumn, the leaves of deciduous trees fall and rot. What does this give to the soil?
qa.a: The rotting leaves give a lot of humus to the soil, so it becomes a fertile brown forest soil.

qa.q: The soils of the Steppes and the Prairies are black and very rich. Why are they called the "granaries of the world"?
qa.a: Their black soil, called chernozem, is very rich in humus from grass roots. Farmers grow huge amounts of wheat on it.

sum.title: II. Soils
sum.intro: The main soils of the temperate region are the following:
items: A. Brown Forest Soils
Under deciduous forests, soils are brown and rich in humus from fallen leaves. They are fertile.
B. Podzols
Under coniferous forests, soils are grey, acidic and poor, because needles rot slowly.
C. Chernozems
Under temperate grasslands, soils are black and very rich in humus. They are the best soils for wheat.
D. Mediterranean Red Soils
In the Mediterranean region, soils are often red (terra rossa) and thin.

evaluation: Why do deciduous trees lose their leaves in autumn?
They lose their leaves to save water during the cold winter, when the ground may freeze.
Give two adaptations of Mediterranean plants to summer drought.
They have small, waxy leaves and long roots.
Why are chernozem soils very fertile?
They are very fertile because they are rich in humus from grass roots.
remediation: Trees that lose their leaves in autumn are called ______ trees.
Trees with needles and cones are called ______ trees.
A typical tree of the Mediterranean region is the ______.
The black, fertile soil of temperate grasslands is called ______.
The grey, acidic soil of coniferous forests is called ______.
The temperate grassland of Argentina is the ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. deciduous 2. coniferous 3. olive 4. chernozem 5. podzol 6. Pampas
